:::{#prp-pmf-density-counting}
#### A PMF is a density with respect to counting measure

If $X$ is a [discrete random variable](#def-discrete-rv) with [PMF](#def-pmf) $f_X$,
and $\measure$ is the [counting measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-measure-spaces.html#def-counting-measure) on $\rangef{X}$,
then $f_X$ is a [density with respect to](#def-density-measure) $\measure$
of the [distribution](#def-cdf) of $X$:
for every [subset](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-subset) $A \subseteq \rangef{X}$,

$$\Pr(X \in A) = \int_A f_X(x)\,d\measure(x)$$

:::

::: proof

The [counting measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-measure-spaces.html#def-counting-measure) is defined on every [subset](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-subset) of $\rangef{X}$,
so every function on $\rangef{X}$ is [measurable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-integrals.html#def-measurable-function),
and $f_X \ge 0$,
because each of its values is a [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability).
The [range](#def-range) $\rangef{X}$ is [countable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-countable-set),
because $X$ is [discrete](#def-discrete-rv),
so each $A \subseteq \rangef{X}$ is countable too,
and the [event](probability-basics.qmd#def-event) $\set{X \in A}$ is the [union](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-union) of the disjoint events $\set{X = x}$ for $x \in A$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(X \in A)
&= \sum_{x \in A} \Pr(X = x)
&& \text{(countable additivity)} \\
&= \sum_{x \in A} f_X(x)
&& \text{(definition of the PMF)} \\
&= \int_A f_X(x)\,d\measure(x)
&& \text{(an integral with respect to counting measure is a sum)}
\ea
$$

The first step is [countable additivity](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-additivity.html#def-countable-additivity),
and the last is the [integral with respect to counting measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-integrals.html#exm-integral-nonneg).

:::
